problem: Situated reasoning relies on pre-explored scenes or active exploration, which is infeasible for physically constrained robots or safety-concerned visually impaired users. No dataset provides temporally consistent imagined video toward a target situation together with reasoning QA along the path.
motivation: Agents often only have a limited current egocentric view, yet must answer spatial 'what-if' questions about unexplored places. World models could act as an imagination engine (emulative simulation, experience-oriented rather than task-oriented instrumental simulation), but no benchmark exists to train and evaluate this.
key_idea: Build WanderDream, a panoramic-video plus QA dataset for emulative simulation, where world models imagine a trajectory from the current view to a target situation and MLLMs reason along the imagined path.
insight: With ground-truth frames, imagination matters more later in the trajectory: start-state questions are best with only s0 (contextual interference), while end-state questions benefit from intermediate frames (s_Δ5 on par with or better than s0+sT). Better-generating world models (lower FVD/End-FID) generally yield better end/path QA, but gains from generated video are small (e.g. ScanNet++ end avg 45.5 -> 47.5), and the GT-frame ablation shows a large gap (ESR 44.4 vs 39.5 for CogVideoX), so generation quality is the bottleneck. Imagination helps most where the anchor is not visible at the start (28.3% of HM3D val).
method: WanderDream-Gen (robot): HM3D object-navigation shortest paths (Habitat-Sim planner; MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN 10°, max 5 m) to 19 landmark classes, rendered as 6-view panoramic RGB/depth/semantic videos of 21 frames (1024x2048).

WanderDream-Gen (human): ScanNet++ situations (interacting/standing/sitting) with start 1.5-3 m away; direct interpolation when clear, otherwise 3D PRM + Dijkstra with capsule validation and micro-PRM repair; random ±30° start head pitch.

WanderDream-QA: 10 questions per video (3 start: object awareness, navigability, ego-target orientation; 4 path: landmark sequencing, spatial estimation, obstacle reasoning, route planning or relative distance change; 3 end: affordance, egocentric spatial relation, object proximity), generated by GPT-5 from Set-of-Mark cubemaps plus trajectory JSON, human-corrected; 158K QA.

Sequential framework: world model (Wan2.1/2.2, HunyuanVideo, CogVideoX1.5) generates the whole panoramic trajectory, either zero-shot with MLLM prompt extension for camera motion or fine-tuned on WanderDream (LoRA / SFT); Qwen3-VL-32B then answers from frames sampled every 5 frames.

Closed-loop framework: MindJourney adaptation where an MLLM proposes step-wise camera actions and SVC synthesizes novel views per question (panoramas split into directional views); evaluated only on the real set.
Metrics: FVD, End-FID, Spherical SSIM, LPIPS for generation; GPT-4o-mini LLM-as-judge 1-5 rating mapped to correctness %, Spearman 0.9722 with humans.
Real-world test set: 26 panoramic head-mounted videos, 182 QA pairs (7 per trajectory) for sim-to-real.

setting.backbone: Video world models (Wan2.1 1.3B, Wan2.2 5B, HunyuanVideo, CogVideoX1.5) fine-tuned with LoRA/SFT or zero-shot with prompt extension; Qwen3-VL-32B / LLaVA-OneVision-1.5-8B frozen few-shot for reasoning
setting.training_data: WanderDream-Gen train: 13,906 videos over 1,000 scenes (ScanNet++ 8,274, HM3D 5,632); LoRA 8 epochs (CogVideoX SFT 10 epochs) at 384x768; MLLMs not trained
setting.observation: single panoramic RGB (equirectangular) start view plus text target-situation description and question
setting.action_space: none (implicit camera control via text/fine-tuning; data paths use forward 0.25 m / turn 10°)
setting.simulator: Habitat-Sim (HM3D), ScanNet++ meshes rendering, real-world captures
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT frames only used in an oracle ablation)

results: Fine-tuned world models improve generation over prompt-extension baselines (Wan2.1 LoRA FVD 5.96 on HM3D vs Wan2.2+PE 17.62) and generated imagination gives modest QA gains on end/path questions (ScanNet++ end 45.5 -> 47.5), but hurts start-state questions. On real data, Wan2.1 LoRA reaches QA 43.0 vs 38.5 without imagination and 31.9 for MindJourney.
limitations: Generation quality is the bottleneck: failures from anchor confusion, occlusion and long-range compression; imagination gains are small compared with GT frames.
Heavy inference latency (Wan 1.3B 35 s, Wan 5B 53 s, HunyuanVideo 211 s, CogVideoX 283 s per trajectory) and a two-stage tool-calling pipeline rather than a unified model.
Shortest-path supervision differs from real human trajectories; real-world test set is small (182 QA, 26 videos); QA is GPT-generated and judged by GPT.
